title: PerLDiff: Controllable Street View Synthesis Using Perspective-Layout Diffusion Model
control_family: layout, box, map or BEV conditioning

output_modality.value: multi-view street-view images (six nuScenes cameras), single frames rather than video; KITTI single-view images

control_signal.value: 3D object annotations (boxes with class and yaw) rendered as perspective layout masking maps, plus road maps; text and camera also used.

control_mechanism.value: PerL-based controlling module with a perspective-layout masked cross-attention, added to pretrained Stable Diffusion and fine-tuned; ConvNext road map encoder; MLP box features; classifier-free guidance.

base_model.value: Pretrained Stable Diffusion v1.4 with PerL-CM; frozen CLIP and ConvNext road map encoder; DDIM sampling, 50 steps.

datasets.value: nuScenes (700 train, 150 validation scenes, 256x384 and 256x704) and KITTI (3,712 train, 3,769 validation images).

metrics.value: FID; perception on generated data: BEVFormer, BEVFusion, StreamPETR detection (mAP, NDS, mAOE), CVT BEV segmentation mIoU, MonoFlex on KITTI.

controllability_evidence.value: BEVFormer on synthetic validation: mAP 25.10, NDS 36.24, mAOE 0.72, versus BEVControl* gains of 8.62% mAP and 8.16% NDS; Road mIoU 61.26, Vehicle mIoU 27.13.

closed_loop.value: No; static image synthesis from annotations, no rollout.

stated_limitations.value: Sometimes generates vehicles with front and rear reversed because the PerL mask ignores 2D orientation; background details can mismatch real images; video generation left to future work.

notes: Image-level controllable street-view generator, not a temporal world model; mentions possible future use as a traffic simulator.
